title: 5 Miami Neighborhoods to Move to if You're Single
igCaption:
Brickell, Wynwood, Edgewater, South Beach and Coconut Grove, with what a typical rental costs in each ZIP right now (Zillow, Aug 2026).

Which one would you pick?

Sources: Zillow Observed Rent Index (August 2026), Wikipedia

#brickell #wynwood #miami #southflorida

scenes.text: If you're single and moving to Miami, these are five neighborhoods you should know about.

Brickell. Miami's financial district and its densest neighborhood, with about forty thousand people packed into towers. Typical rent in the thirty-three one thirty-one ZIP is three thousand eight hundred thirty-one dollars.
scenes.caption: Brickell. Miami's financial district and its densest neighborhood, with about 40,000 people packed into towers. Typical rent in the 33131 ZIP is $3,831.

scenes.text: Wynwood. Old warehouses turned into murals, breweries, restaurants and clubs. Rent in the thirty-three one twenty-seven ZIP averages two thousand nine hundred fifty-six, up seventy-two percent since twenty nineteen.
scenes.caption: Wynwood. Old warehouses turned into murals, breweries, restaurants and clubs. Rent in the 33127 ZIP averages $2,956, up 72% since 2019.

scenes.text: Edgewater. High-rises along Biscayne Bay, a few minutes from the Design District and Downtown. Typical rent here is three thousand five hundred seventy-two.
scenes.caption: Edgewater. High-rises along Biscayne Bay, a few minutes from the Design District and Downtown. Typical rent here is $3,572.

scenes.text: South Beach. The surprise is the price. The thirty-three one thirty-nine ZIP averages two thousand eight hundred thirty-five, the cheapest on this list, with the beach and Ocean Drive right outside.
scenes.caption: South Beach. The surprise is the price. The 33139 ZIP averages $2,835, the cheapest on this list, with the beach and Ocean Drive right outside.

scenes.text: And Coconut Grove, Miami's oldest neighborhood, full of trees, bayfront bars and marinas. It's also the fastest riser here. Rent has more than doubled since twenty fifteen, from seventeen seventy-five to three thousand six hundred twenty-one.
scenes.caption: And Coconut Grove, Miami's oldest neighborhood, full of trees, bayfront bars and marinas. It's also the fastest riser here. Rent has more than doubled since 2015, from $1,775 to $3,621.
